name: Monarchism in Brazil
summary: Brazilian monarchism seeks to restore a hereditary constitutional monarchy under the Orleans-Braganza Imperial House, modeled on the parliamentary empire of Pedro II. The Emperor would be a non-partisan head of state holding the moderating power, while a Prime Minister backed by an elected two-chamber Parliament governs. Its stated program is also socially conservative and Catholic-inflected, stressing the family, subsidiarity, strong armed forces and national reconciliation, and it leaves economic policy to elected governments.
scope: The contemporary mainstream of organized monarchism (the Vassouras line of Prince Bertrand and the Pro Monarquia campaign), based on its 'Propostas Basicas' platform approved in 1991 and revised in 2023, plus Wikipedia accounts of the movement and the Empire. It excludes the Petropolis branch (whose current head declared himself republican), the authoritarian Patrianovist monarchism of the 1930s, and the Tradition-Family-Property ideological milieu as such. Many economic and international statements are inferred because the platform deliberately defines no government program.

keyFigures.name: Prince Bertrand of Orleans-Braganza
keyFigures.role: Head of the Vassouras branch of the Imperial House since 2022 and recognized by the movement as the legitimate claimant.

keyFigures.name: Pedro II of Brazil
keyFigures.role: Last emperor, whose parliamentary reign is the movement's model.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The platform asks for the broadest media freedom (B6) yet wants legal protection of honor and family morality, so adherents are split on restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: The Emperor is head of state, not government (intro, A3); the executive sits with a Prime Minister who needs Parliament's confidence, so bypassing gridlock by a strongman is not the model.

state-harmful.rationale: The platform builds a full state: Parliament, judiciary, Council of State, armed forces and police (A, B3-B4); it is plainly not anarchist.

empower-police-military.rationale: B3 and B4 call for valuing and supporting the armed forces, military police and civil police, with proper conditions and recognition.

decide-locally.rationale: A7 keeps federalism and A8 expands municipal autonomy, so decisions move toward local levels, though the national Crown stays.

rehabilitation.rationale: No penal philosophy is stated; Christian outlook supports reform, order-minded outlook supports punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: B1 calls the family the mother cell of society and the foundation of Christian civilization, and C2 models monarchy itself on the family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Follows from the Catholic doctrine the platform and its defenders link to monarchism (B1, s4) rather than from an explicit statement. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

abortion-legal.rationale: B1 asks for protecting the life of offspring and an anti-infanticide consciousness in every home; Catholic doctrine on this is firm.

more-religion-public.rationale: B1 names Christian civilization as the basis of society, and a prominent defender ties monarchism to Catholic doctrine (s4).

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents honor the 1888 abolition by Princess Isabel (s3) but the platform does not address present remedies, so views split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement frames the Crown as symbol of national unity and continuity with the Empire that assured Brazil's unity and greatness (C1).

gradual-change.rationale: The plan restores the 1824 Constitution with needed adaptations to present reality (A1) and keeps judicial and federal institutions (A5, A7).

revolution-justified.rationale: The platform insists the restoration campaign be conducted at a high level, aimed at ideas not people (C2), and modern monarchists seek a plebiscite; historic revolts (s2) failed and are not the program.

experts-over-public.rationale: A Council of State of eminent figures chosen by the Emperor (A6) gives experts an advisory role, but Parliament is elected by universal suffrage (A4).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic policy is explicitly left to the Prime Minister's government (intro), so the movement itself holds no tariff position.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Catholic social thought favors cooperation, but the platform uses free unions (B5) and an elected Parliament (A4).

one-party-rule.rationale: A4 and A3 establish a Parliament elected by universal suffrage and a Prime Minister with its confidence; C2 treats parties as legitimate participants in debate.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: A1 and A2 call for restoring a hereditary monarchy under the Imperial House.

democracy-best.rationale: The proposed monarchy is parliamentary with universal-suffrage elections (A3-A4), though adherents argue the monarchy improves on republican democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: The model is representative parliamentarism (A3-A4); direct decisions are used only for plebiscites on new states (A7).

workers-councils.rationale: Incompatible with the bicameral elected Parliament in A4.

right-to-secede.rationale: C1 calls for national union around the heir of the emperors who secured Brazil's unity; A7 allows only new states made within the federation by plebiscite.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholic natural-law tradition shapes values, but the platform does not base law on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A5 protects an independent public judiciary and B3-B4 give defense and police to the state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: C1-C2 call for reconciliation of all Brazilians, forgetting divisions, on the family model.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The platform has no indigenous policy; Imperial-era tradition and present conservative views point in different directions.

limit-population.rationale: B1 values the life of the offspring and the family; population limitation conflicts with it. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A technical privacy question absent from monarchist writings; order-minded and liberty-minded adherents would split.

restore-past-order.rationale: The program is itself a restoration of the 1824 constitutional order (A1), though adapted to current realities.

direct-action.rationale: The platform channels change through ideas and a plebiscite (C2, s4), not street action.

means-match-ends.rationale: C2 wants a campaign that reflects the harmony of the desired monarchy.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly foreign to a program that restores a parliamentary state with a bicameral legislature and courts (A3-A5).

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist framing absent from the platform; the movement leaves economic organization to ordinary parliamentary politics (intro).

profit-exploitation.rationale: Contrary to the class-harmony view in C1-C2; not explicitly debated.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejects class struggle and rests on a parliament elected by all (A4, C2).

taxation-theft.rationale: The program assumes a functioning state financing forces, courts and teachers (A5, B2-B3).

harm-principle.rationale: B1 and B6 allow law to defend family and social morality, going beyond harm to others.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Parliament elected by universal suffrage (A4) is the main check, not exit.

organic-representation.rationale: A4 elects Parliament by universal suffrage and A3 uses parliamentary confidence, not corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: B2 applies subsidiarity: family educates first and the state only completes what is needed.

national-rebirth.rationale: C1 calls for a union of living forces to overcome grave crises, but not for a radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Program defends national territory (B3) but not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Emperor rules within constitutional law and Parliament (A3), not through personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Slavery was abolished by Princess Isabel (s3) and nothing in the program restores bonded labor.

single-common-good.rationale: C1 urges a sacred union of Brazilian forces around one throne, implying one national good.

school-vouchers.rationale: B2 says the state must develop the private school network and supplement it with public schools, which is close to vouchers. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

rule-by-example.rationale: C2 casts monarchy on the family model, with the sovereign as moral example.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The whole program restores inherited institutions and symbols (A1, A2).

workers-nation.rationale: The class-or-nation question is not posed in the program; C1-C2 national union leaves it open at best.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The imperial tradition ended slavery in 1888 (s3) and C1 unites all Brazilians; segregation has no place.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are absent from the platform; adherents plausibly split.

proportional-representation.rationale: A4 sets universal-suffrage elections for both chambers without naming a system.

national-mission.rationale: The program is domestic (A-C); no mission to export a form of government is stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: A defender argues presidents think of the next election while a monarch is above party interests, and says Brazil has been unstable since 1889.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: B1 defends the life of offspring and family; Catholic doctrine opposes eugenics. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The program has the state also complete education (B2) and uphold family morality (B6).

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: C1 calls on all Brazilians to unite; the monarchy is idealized as a family.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: B2 stresses family educational authority and Christian civilization.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine unrelated to the platform; implausible for adherents.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents seek a plebiscite and a parliament with universal suffrage (A4, s4), though the Crown's legitimacy is also hereditary.

population-transfer.rationale: C2 asks reconciliation of all Brazilians without hatreds or persecution of persons.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The platform backs armed forces and police (B3-B4), so an absolute rule is not clear.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican-theory formulation not used in monarchist sources; with a hereditary head of state, adherents would not obviously accept it.

separated-powers.rationale: The plan has a bicameral legislature, a PM-led executive, an independent judiciary (A5) and the Emperor's moderating power (A3).

vanguard-party.rationale: Opposed to class struggle and revolutionary politics (C1-C2).

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic-inspired concern, but not in the platform.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy with no Brazilian monarchist treatment.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: C1 calls for unity but nothing links it to diversity; adherents plausibly split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to the platform's Emperor-appointed Council of State (A6) and elected Parliament (A4).

party-controls-media.rationale: B6 says media should have the broadest powers to inform and shape opinion, as under Pedro II.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No pay limit proposed; the platform keeps a conventional elected Parliament (A4).

head-commands-forces.rationale: The current platform (A3) has a Prime Minister governing with parliamentary confidence, while the 1824 model it honours gave the Emperor executive and moderating power; the movement does not settle who should command the forces.

clerical-rule.rationale: Government is by Emperor and Parliament (A3-A4), not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: B3 honors the armed forces as guardians of the Nation; class-based defeatism is at odds with C1.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: B6 asks for protection of family and social morality yet wide media freedom.

people-in-arms.rationale: B3-B4 rely on professional forces and police as reserves.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not a theme of the program; some Catholic-traditionalist writers say yes but the sources do not.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: B2 gives family primary duty for educating children.

restrict-pornography.rationale: B6 asks for legal defense of family and social morality in media.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A dependency-theory claim absent from monarchist sources; the platform seeks restoration of political institutions only.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The plan restores the 1824 constitution via plebiscite (A1, s4), not a new assembly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A2 makes the head of state hereditary in the Imperial House.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not in the platform; mild conservative inference only.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A leftist debate that monarchist sources do not engage; adherents just reject Soviet communism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Movement is tied to Catholic doctrine (s4); program wants Christian civilization (B1).

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A3 makes the Emperor head of state, not government, holding the moderating power above the Prime Minister (intro).

sacred-ruler.rationale: Constitutional model with a ruler bound by Parliament (A3); divine descent not claimed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is left to the PM's government; the platform states no preference.

character-from-environment.rationale: An abstract theory-of-human-nature question not treated; family upbringing is emphasised (B1) but innate nature is also assumed in Catholic thought.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A defender stresses the monarch is subject to the laws (s4), and the model is constitutional (A1).

mixed-constitution.rationale: Hereditary Crown, appointed Council of State (A6), and elected two-chamber Parliament (A4) mix elements.

leader-cult.rationale: The Emperor is a constitutional symbol; C2 focuses on ideas not persons.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question outside monarchist concern.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentist claims are not part of the program; Brazil has no such claims.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A diaspora-politics question that does not arise for Brazilian monarchism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is absent from the program.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: A5 secures judges' life tenure, irremovability and salary, to keep the judiciary independent.

moral-incentives.rationale: A socialist concept not found in monarchist writings; no lean.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: C2 wants the campaign waged at a high level aimed at ideas.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: A2 restores a hereditary monarchy and the Imperial House.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A Marxist-debate question; conservative adherents would lean yes but nothing is stated.

delink-world-market.rationale: A dependency-theory prescription absent from monarchist sources.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The restoration keeps an adapted 1824 constitution (A1); amendment rules are not specified.

elective-rulers.rationale: A2 makes succession hereditary within the Imperial House.

minority-veto.rationale: The plan relies on Parliament and PM confidence (A3-A4); a minority veto is alien to that.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Emperor is not head of government and the PM needs Parliament's confidence (A3), though the Emperor keeps the moderating power.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: C1 calls for a national union and engagement.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist-party question with no monarchist counterpart.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A U.S. historiographical dispute with no bearing on Brazilian monarchism; no lean.

military-guardian-role.rationale: B3 calls the armed forces guardians of the Nation, on whom social peace and security rest. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The 1824 Constitution gave the General Assembly control of taxes and spending (s3), which the restoration follows (A1).

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: A Cold War doctrine with no relevance for the monarchist program.

industrial-unions.rationale: B5 commits only to free unionism, not any union structure.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: B1 calls family the foundation of Christian civilization.

religious-nation.rationale: C1 calls all Brazilians; not religion-defined.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A tributary-system concept foreign to Brazilian monarchism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Statement presupposes common ownership of production; not part of program.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: B2 envisions public schools complementing a strong private network.

religion-illusion.rationale: B1 sees Christian civilization as foundational.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist-feminist claim; opposed in spirit by B1 but not directly discussed.

socialized-care.rationale: B1-B2 put childcare and education chiefly in the family.

suppress-opposition.rationale: C2 declares the campaign will not target persons, organizations or parties, and A4 has an elected Parliament.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A Salafi-jihadi proposition foreign to Brazilian monarchism.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: An intersectional framework opposed by the platform's class-harmony and family framing.

assisted-dying.rationale: B1 emphasizes protecting life; Catholic doctrine inference.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept absent from monarchist sources.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: B3 stresses the great mission of the armed forces as guardians of the Nation.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: No foreign-alliance position in the program.

dynastic-succession.rationale: A2 calls for hereditary monarchy in the Imperial House.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not in monarchist sources; opposed to conventional banking assumptions.

property-franchise.rationale: A4 elects both chambers by universal suffrage.

racial-franchise.rationale: A4 gives universal suffrage; C1 unites all Brazilians.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: C2 explicitly seeks reconciliation without hatreds; no support for boycotts.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The platform honors the armed forces (B3) and defends traditional family values (B1) but does not discuss who may serve.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: B1 grounds society in Christian civilization; state atheism is unthinkable for adherents.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: B4 gives police, military police and civil police an irreplaceable role in order and security.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not part of the program; C2 favours reconciliation, not drilled youth.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Strict pacifism is absent; the program honors the forces and police (B3-B4).

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: C2 calls the restoration a national crusade, a hint of spiritual framing but not an explicit doctrine.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A Zionism-diaspora question with no monarchist counterpart.

independent-unions.rationale: B5 commits to free unionism per the ILO charter.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist definition dispute with no monarchist counterpart.

confederal-coordination.rationale: A8 expands municipal autonomy within states, but not a confederation.

second-chamber.rationale: A4 states a bicameral legislature of Senate and Chamber of Deputies.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Digital-currency privacy is a question the platform never touches; it only values police effectiveness (B4).

online-anonymity.rationale: Internet policy is absent from the sources; B6 only asks for broad media freedom with a right to defend honor.

person-over-state.rationale: B2 subsidiarity puts the family's educational mission before the state.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A7 keeps federalism; Parliament may only split units by plebiscite.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning and environmental trade-offs are absent from the monarchist program.

communal-electorates.rationale: Opposed since A4 calls for universal suffrage in one electorate.

future-generations.rationale: A defender says monarchs think of the next generation (s4).

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: B3-B4 assign defense and security to armed forces, military police and civil police.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: B3 honors the forces as guardians of the Nation.

collective-bargaining.rationale: B5 commits to free unionism but sets no bargaining model.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Income-support design is left to elected governments under the parliamentary model (intro); nothing is stated.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The program restores existing institutions (A1, A5).

sacred-nation.rationale: C1 speaks of a sacred union around the Crown.

party-commands-army.rationale: B3 makes the armed forces guardians of the Nation, and the Emperor holds the moderating power above party government (A3).

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not a concern for Brazil, a single state; no monarchist source treats divided nations.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: B6 says media should enjoy broad freedom as under Pedro II, implying the press is not a sham.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The platform stresses strong armed forces but does not address nuclear weapons, and Brazil's constitution bars them; neutral.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Platform leaves policy to elected governments and subsidiarity could favour either route; neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Empire had an established Catholic religion while the modern platform is Catholic-inflected but accepts religious freedom; adherents split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The platform deliberately defines no government economic program, so neutral.

simple-living.rationale: Simple self-sufficient living is not a program topic; an economics-neutral platform leaves it to individuals.

close-ties-china.rationale: The platform deliberately defines no foreign economic programme and leaves such choices to elected governments.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The platform leaves economic policy to elected governments; subsidiarity points to neither targeted nor universal provision.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The platform proposes a Prime Minister backed by an elected two-chamber Parliament under a non-partisan Emperor, so parties and representative institutions are central, not obstacles.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The platform is Catholic-inflected but defines a constitutional state; the sources do not show a stand on denominational politics.

multipolar-world.rationale: The platform leaves international questions undefined; adherents tend to value sovereignty and strong armed forces, but no multipolar stance is documented.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: A hereditary constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament and a socially conservative platform is opposed to a communist-led socialist system.

missingStatements.text: The head of state should hold a neutral moderating power to arbitrate between the executive, legislative and judicial branches.
missingStatements.rationale: A3 of the platform assigns the moderating power to the Emperor as a defining feature of the restored monarchy, and the 1824 constitution created it as a separate branch.

missingStatements.text: Judges and prosecutors should hold life tenure and be irremovable so that they stay independent.
missingStatements.rationale: A5 of the platform keeps life tenure, irremovability and irreducible salaries for judges and prosecutors.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to life tenure of judges under a restored monarchy; too narrow for the bank.

notes: The platform leaves government programs to the Prime Minister, so economic, international and many social answers are low-confidence inferences from its Catholic-conservative framing. The Petropolis branch and some adherents differ, and the 1930s Patrianovists were authoritarian. The Gazeta do Povo source was read through a summarizing fetch tool.
